mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as high inflation erodes corporate profit margins and consumer purchasing power.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and fall in employment (PAYEMS) over the past month predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to a deteriorating labor market signaling economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 0.2pp increase in 1 month AND PAYEMS < -100000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp and PAYEMS falls by more than 100,000 in the past month, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS above 3.5% and sustained for 3 months), S&P 500 predicts negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS has been above 3.5% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing market (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as strong housing activity indicates a healthy economy and rising consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances where HOUST increased over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units in the past month predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to a weak housing market signaling economic contraction.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances where HOUST falls below 1200, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) rises and housing starts (HOUST) fall over the past month, it predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days because a strong industrial sector without a strong housing market indicates economic imbalance and vulnerability to recession.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% increase in 1 month AND HOUST < 0.5% decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances where INDPRO rises by more than 0.5% and HOUST falls by more than 0.5% in the past month, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDPC1 YoY growth above 3.0% and UNRATE below 4.5%), S&P 500 predicts positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to strong economic growth and corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in < 40% of instances where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 3.0% and UNRATE is below 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
